proof_summary: An odd integer with totient a power of two is shown to be a squarefree product of Fermat primes, with the totient exponent equal to the sum of their distinct power-of-two indices; hence a sum equal to $2^{33}$ forces the sole factor to be $F_{33}$. Using $\varphi(m)<m$ and the decomposition of $m$ into its $2$-part and odd part, any admissible $m<2^{2^{33}+1}$ must therefore equal the prime $F_{33}$, while the general lower bound and $\varphi(2^{2^{33}+1})=2^{2^{33}}$ establish the two cases.
